questions.q: Why can't a large pretraining run simply start at its peak learning rate from step zero?
options: GPUs cannot process a high learning rate at initialization
Random initial weights and not-yet-settled optimizer moment estimates make early steps at a high rate likely to push the model out of a stable region
The tokenizer has not finished loading at step zero
Peak learning rate is only defined after warmup finishes
questions.explain: At initialization, weights are random and Adam-family optimizers' adaptive estimates aren't reliable yet, so an immediate high learning rate risks destabilizing early training.

options: Holds the learning rate at its peak value for the entire run
Ramps the learning rate from near zero up to its target peak value over the first N steps
Decays the learning rate to zero immediately
Doubles the batch size every step
questions.explain: Linear warmup increases the learning rate linearly from near zero to the target peak over a defined number of initial steps, before any decay phase begins.

questions.q: Which Hugging Face `transformers` helper implements a warmup-then-cosine-decay learning-rate schedule?
options: AutoModelForCausalLM
get_cosine_schedule_with_warmup
BitsAndBytesConfig
SFTTrainer
questions.explain: get_cosine_schedule_with_warmup wraps a PyTorch optimizer and implements linear warmup followed by cosine decay, returned as a standard LR scheduler.

questions.q: How is peak learning rate typically chosen relative to model size?
options: It is always the same fixed value regardless of model size
Larger models generally use somewhat smaller peak learning rates, often informed by small-scale sweeps
Peak learning rate is chosen randomly for each run
It is irrelevant to training stability
questions.explain: Peak learning rate is generally scaled down as model size grows, informed by published configurations and small-scale learning-rate sweeps extrapolated to the target size.

questions.q: What is warmup-stable-decay (WSD), and why might a team prefer it over cosine decay?
options: A schedule that decays immediately with no warmup phase
A schedule that holds a constant peak rate for most of training and decays sharply only near the end, allowing the token budget to be extended without a pre-committed total step count
A schedule used only for fine-tuning, never pretraining
A synonym for linear warmup
questions.explain: WSD holds a constant learning rate through most of training and only decays near the end, giving teams flexibility to extend training length without having baked a fixed total into a cosine curve.
